definitions.explanation: A bridge made of iron or steel, especially one designed to carry railway tracks. Also used for any metal bridge.

examples.japanese: ⟦{電車|でんしゃ}→電車：00522_densha⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{鉄橋|てっきょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{渡|わた}っている→渡る：02441_wataru⟧。
examples.english: A train is crossing the railway bridge.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧{鉄橋|てっきょう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{百年|ひゃくねん}→百年：28401_hyakunen⟧{以上前|いじょうまえ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{造|つく}られた→造る：17751_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: This iron bridge was built over a hundred years ago.

examples.japanese: ⟦{大|おお}きな→大きな：02849_ookina⟧{鉄橋|てっきょう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{上|うえ}→上：00682_ue⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{貨物|かもつ}{列車|れっしゃ}→貨物列車：16297_kamotsuressha⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{轟音|ごうおん}→轟音：14309_gouon⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{立|た}てて→立てる：01196_tateru⟧⟦{通過|つうか}した→通過する：22435_tsuukasuru⟧。
examples.english: A freight train passed over the large railway bridge with a thundering roar.

notes:
USAGE:
{鉄橋|てっきょう} typically refers to a bridge carrying railway tracks, though it can mean any bridge made of iron or steel. It often evokes images of classic industrial-era infrastructure.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鉄橋|てっきょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{渡|わた}る→渡る：02441_wataru⟧ (to cross a railway bridge)
- {鉄橋|てっきょう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{上|うえ}→上：00682_ue⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{走|はし}る→走る：00519_hashiru⟧ (to run across a bridge)
- {鉄橋|てっきょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{架|か}ける (to build a bridge)

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{橋|はし}→橋：02163_hashi⟧: bridge (general)
- {陸橋|りっきょう}: overpass, footbridge
- {石橋|いしばし}: stone bridge
- {吊|つ}り{橋|ばし}: suspension bridge
